top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards the invention of the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock (Katori) and its realisation at the 1e-18 level (Ye) with a two-name allocation and a citation scope that is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. The science is mature and reproduced across independent laboratories, and it already enables measurements no earlier standard could make. Credit boundaries (Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Sterr, Gill) are a real reservation but not decisive. P002 is a genuine discovery but less mature, with the pairing mechanism unsettled and experimental credit incomplete, so it ranks second; a prize this year is still preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented tie to Katori or Ye, and my documented collaborators (Gothenburg group, L'Huillier, Lund attosecond group, Keller's group at ETH, Schuch, Dahlstrom, Argenti, Indelicato) are not on the slate, though I work in the same atomic-physics community
